answer: To resist Sybil attacks, each network vertex must continuously evaluate a memory-hard verifiable delay function and submit epoch proofs. Because the sequential steps match peak core speeds, one execution thread cannot time-slice multiple identities without missing deadlines, imposing real costs in dedicated silicon, memory bandwidth, and power per identity. However, attackers can exploit a cloud spot-price nadir to cheaply rent idle servers for short Sybil bursts.
